title: What If Every Mangrove Forest Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every mangrove forest vanished? The storms would arrive first.
Mangroves slow waves and storm surge, cutting flood risk for about 15 million people every year.
They also shield roughly 65 billion dollars of property each year, according to an IUCN assessment.
Their soil holds more than 21 billion tons of carbon dioxide, across the 147,000 square kilometers that remain.
Clear them, and carbon stored in that wet soil can return to the air.
They are already shrinking: over 5,000 square kilometers were lost between 1996 and 2020. Without them, the coast loses its first line of defense.

description:
What if every mangrove forest disappeared?
They protect about 15 million people from flooding each year and hold billions of tons of carbon dioxide.
